title: Charcoal pod rot (Diplodia pod rot) of Cocoa

Header: Charcoal pod rot (Diplodia pod rot) of Cocoa

Prevention: Avoid the wounding of cherelles (young pods) and pods during farm operations such as weeding and harvesting.
Ensure proper farm husbandary practices, weeding, pruning etc.
Ensure proper nutrition of cacao trees through fertilization (Conact
Avoid transporting infected pods to uninfected areas
Monitoring: Look out for pods with sooty black powdery substance (fungal spores).
When infected pods are touched, a black charcoal-like substance is left on the fingers.
Monitor field all year round, but very conspicuous when trees are stressed in the dry season
Direct Control: Remove or harvest infected pods as soon as observed
Restrictions: This disease is of low economic importance and no chemical control measures are advised for its management
